title: Rebind complete latent-ceiling claims to validated corpus identity
finding: evaluate() accepted an in-memory Corpus dataclass directly. The frozen source-revision and denominator guards prevented simple identity changes from completing, but a directly constructed Corpus with the frozen identifiers and 1,383 measured rows could bypass Corpus.parse invariants such as unique item ids and retained corpus_sha256 binding, allowing malformed or stale in-memory evidence to reach the numeric-ceiling path.
primary_claim: A candidate complete latent-ceiling result is now rebound to the canonical evidence payload and revalidated through the existing Corpus.parse path before any numeric ceiling is emitted. Duplicate/malformed rows or a stale corpus identity therefore fail closed instead of becoming complete evidence.
gardener_decision: Reuse the existing Corpus.parse and Row.parse validation path by reconstructing the exact canonical evidence payload only when an input is otherwise eligible to publish a final ceiling. Do not duplicate row validators, add a constructor-token framework, introduce a second evidence model, or build latent/Tensor infrastructure.
acceptance: a parser-created complete measured corpus on the frozen source revision and denominator still computes present_not_expressible / 1383
a directly constructed complete corpus with duplicate item ids is refused through the existing parser invariant before a numeric ceiling is emitted
a directly constructed complete corpus whose corpus_sha256 does not bind its exact validated semantics is refused before a numeric ceiling is emitted
non-frozen source revisions and denominators remain incomplete rather than being promoted into final claims
the committed prediction-only corpus remains byte-identical, valid, incomplete, and unable to emit a numeric ceiling
no OwnerApproval, promotion, gate transition, or benchmark superiority claim is created
